description: The table gives the number of lights, daymarks, fog signals and signal stations under government and public control at the end of 1914, as the text introduces the planned new lighthouses.

description: Gives the yearly output of lacquer-juice and lacquered wares from 1913 to 1915, following the text on the lacquer industry's centres and uses.

title: [Sake, Beer and Soy Production, Years Ended March 1913–1916]
description: Following the discussion of soy brewing, this table gives the output of sake, beer and soy in koku for the years ended March 1913 to 1916.

title: Fish-Oil Output
description: Gives the yearly output of sardine, herring and whale oil in koku and yen, with other oils and totals, shown after the note on the fish-oil industry.

title: [Gas Lamps, Installations and Production]
description: Shows the relative proportion of gas used for lighting, heating and motor purposes, with gas volume produced, as electricity encroaches on the gas industry's lighting business.

title: [Kilowatt in Operation of Electric Enterprises, 1910–1915]
description: Shows the growing kilowatt capacity in operation of electric enterprises by type of plant from 1910 to 1915, illustrating the rapid development of electric industry.

title: [Productions of Straw, Chip and Hemp Braid]
description: Shows yearly production values of straw, chip, mixed and hemp braid, presented to illustrate how the braid industry developed after the Russo-Japanese war.

title: [Leather Output Statistics]
description: Gives the annual value of leather output by source (cows and calves, horses, others) from 1912 to 1915, presented as statistics of leather output in the hides and leathers discussion.

title: [Hosiery Production]
description: Shows Osaka-centred hosiery output by product for 1912 to 1915, illustrating the wartime boom in the industry.

title: Production (¥1.0000)
description: Gives the value of Japan's canned goods production by type for 1913 to 1915, to show the growing canning industry.

title: [Isinglass Production]
description: Gives the yearly quantity and value of Japanese isinglass (kanten) production for the years ended March 1913 to 1916.

title: Composition of Prefectures
description: Shows, for six prefectures, their governor and the number of gun, cities, towns and villages, illustrating how Japan's prefectures are subdivided for administration.

title: Cities and Mayors
description: Gives the names of the mayors of the listed cities, arranged in two columns, as a companion to the prefectural list.

title: [Cities and Their Mayors]
description: A list of the cities of Japan with the name of each city's mayor, given for reference in the administrative section of the year book.

title: Shin-nin Rank
description: Lists the annual salaries of the Shin-nin (senior) rank officials, showing the pay attached to each high government post.

title: Choku-nin Rank
description: Gives the annual salaries of Choku-nin (higher official) rank posts, including local governors, with a note on extra allowances for certain prefectures.
labels: Chief Sec., Houses of the Diet

title: Military Service
description: Shows pensions, family annuities and retiring grants paid to military officers and their families for 1911 to 1915, continuing the civil service record.
headers: Annuity to family — No. of recipients

title: Government of Karafuto
description: Names the governor of the Karafuto administration within the directory of civil and military service.

title: Board of Audit
description: Names the president and sectional chiefs of the Board of Audit within the directory of civil and military service.
examples: K. Hama (1st Sec.), K. Nakakuma (2nd Sec.)

title: Court of Administrative Litigation
description: Names the president and councillors of the Court of Administrative Litigation within the directory of civil and military service.
examples: Dr. R. Watanabe, Dr. S. Koba, S. Kubota, Dr. Shimizu, K. Sekiguchi, T. Miyake, T. Shimada, T. Shimamura, E. Yadori, E. Baba, H. Futakami, Dr. G. Endo, S. Matsumura, M. Iwata.

title: Divisional Commanders
description: Lists the commanding Lieutenant-Generals of each standing army division, giving the division names and their commanders.

title: Commanders of Infantry Brigades
description: Shows the Major-Generals commanding each infantry brigade, arranged by division, as part of the list of standing army and garrison commanders.

title: Commanders of Cavalry Brigades
description: Names the Major-Generals commanding the cavalry brigades attached to the Guards, 1st, 8th and 15th divisions.

title: Commanders of Heavy Artillery Brigades
description: Lists the Army officers commanding the heavy artillery brigades, by division and brigade, with the Major-General in charge of each.

title: Commanders of Heavy Artillery Brigade
description: Gives the officers commanding the single heavy artillery brigades listed for the 1st and 12th Divisions.

title: Commander of Communication Corps
description: Names the commander of the Communication Corps attached to the Guards Division.

title: Commanders of Garrisons and Forts
description: Lists the garrison and fort commanders across Japan, Korea, Formosa, Kwantung and China, with each officer's rank and name.

title: Admiralties
description: Gives the senior staff of the four naval admiralties (Yokosuka, Kure, Sasebo, Maizuru), the navy's main dockyard commands, with their ranks and names.

title: Japanese in Korea
description: Gives the yearly Japanese population in Korea from 1912 to 1914, following the note that Japanese settlers had grown rapidly since the 1904-5 war.

title: Foreigners in Korea
description: Shows the number of foreign residents in Korea by nationality for 1912 to 1914, given alongside the Japanese population figures.

title: [Prefectures, Seats of Office and Governors of Korea]
description: The page lists the thirteen provinces of Korea under the Government-General, with the seat of office and the Japanese or Korean governor of each.

title: Continuing Expenditure
description: Lists the Korean public works funded by continuing loan-programme expenditure approved by the Diet in 1910-11, with completion years and estimated sums.
labels: New Wiju street and river repair

title: Debts of Chosen (Sept. 1915)
description: Shows the outstanding loans and bonds of the Chosen (Korean) government as of September 1915, with issue year, amount, interest rate and redemption period.

title: Traffic Results
description: Shows annual traffic results of the Chosen Government Railways for 1913 to 1915 in passengers, luggage, goods and receipts, illustrating the railway's operating performance.

title: [Average Per Mile Per Day Traffic Figures]
description: Gives the average per mile per day figures for passengers, goods and receipts on the Chosen Government Railways for 1913 to 1915.

title: Principal Cities at the End of 1914
description: Populations of the principal cities of Taiwan at the end of 1914, listed in two columns.

title: [Record of Raids by the Aborigines]
description: Shows the yearly number of aborigines killed and wounded in raids from 1909 to 1913, split between police and other officers and people, as background to the subjugation campaigns.

title: Justice
description: Civil and criminal case loads of the first-instance courts and courts of appeal for December 1912 to 1914, showing cases brought, disposed of and remaining.

title: [Stamps and Shakujime by Species at Arisan]
description: The table lists the estimated number of stamps and the yield in shakujime for the principal timber species in the Arisan forest.

title: Area of Cultivation
description: Shows the cultivated area of paddy, upland, and various crops in Formosa for 1913 to 1915, as a basis for the island's agricultural production.
headers: Area of plantations — Beans, pease etc.

title: Principal Crops
description: Gives the annual output of the principal crops of Formosa, such as rice, rush, ground-nut and jute, for 1913 to 1915.

title: [Sugar Area and Output in Formosa, 1911–1916]
description: Presents the sugar-cane area and sugar output in Formosa from 1911 to 1916, showing the development of the sugar industry after Japanese rule.

title: [Tea Production]
description: Shows Formosa's wrapper tea production by season and year, 1912 to 1915, given in the tea section as the amount produced in 1000 kin.

title: [Mineral Fields, December 1914 and 1915]
description: Introduces the island's main mineral fields by measured area, showing gold, copper, coal and petroleum sites at the end of 1914 and 1915.

title: Three Principal Cities at the End of 1914
description: Shows the male, female and total population of the three principal cities of the leased territory at the end of 1914.

title: Business Report for 1916-7 Year
description: The Japan Year Book reports the South Manchuria Railway Company's business results for 1916-7, showing receipts and expenses by undertaking and the overall profit.

title: Assets and Liabilities
description: Principal asset and liability items from the company's business report, listed by category, accompanying the 1916-7 business summary.

title: List of Mikados in Alphabetical Order
description: An alphabetical index of the Mikados, giving each sovereign's reign dates so readers can locate a ruler's period quickly in the historical outline.

title: [Reigns of the Mikados]
description: The list gives the dates of each Mikado's reign, showing the sovereigns in order, with pre-Christian reigns marked B.C. and female and Northern Court sovereigns flagged.

title: List of the Shoguns and the Regents (Shikken)
description: The table lists the Shoguns and the Shikken Regents by family line, giving the years each held office, for reference on the Japanese shogunates.

title: List of Japanese "Year-Names"
description: A list of Japanese year-names (nengō) in four columns, each giving the romanised name, its kanji, and the Western years in which it began and ended, as an aid to dating events in Japanese history.

title: [Japanese Era Names with Romanized and Kanji Forms and Years]
description: A chronological list of Japanese era names (nengō) in romanized and kanji form, each with its starting and ending years, provided as a reference for dating events in Japanese history.

title: Cases of Insolvency and Rehabilitation
description: Reports yearly insolvency cases with numbers of debtors and creditors, credit amounts and rehabilitation outcomes from 1911 to 1915.

title: Capital Punishment Classified
description: Gives the number of persons executed for murder, burglary and offences against the Imperial Court in each year from 1910 to 1915.

title: Data at the End of March 1917
description: Shows the mutual relief insurance arrangement for workmen in five Government establishments at the end of March 1917, covering membership, receipts, disbursements and persons helped.

title: [Monthly Living Expenses of Workpeople, Tokyo, May 1916]
description: Breaks down the monthly living expenses of 20 labor families from Prof. Iwano's May 1916 survey, by item and in total.

title: Child Operatives
description: Lists the number of child operatives under 15 by sex and age in the match, glass and filature factories employing the largest shares of child labour.

title: [Female Factory Operatives by Age and Sex]
description: Shows the number of male and female factory workers under 12 and aged 12–15 in four industries, with totals, illustrating the female operative conditions discussed in the surrounding text.

title: [Operatives at Government Works by Sex and Age, End of 1916]
description: Shows the number of male and female operatives at government works by age group at the end of 1916, illustrating the treatment of workers there.

title: Numer of Operatives
description: Number of factory operatives in 1916, classified by sex and type of factory, for factories employing at least 10,000 persons.

title: Press Statistics
description: Compiled by the Police Bureau, this table gives the number of dailies and periodicals, with and without deposit, existing at the end of 1915 and 1916.

title: [Operatives at Government Works by Sex and Age, End of 1916]
description: Gives the number of male and female operatives, by age group, at Government factories at the end of 1916 to show the share of child workers.

title: [Civil Engineering Expenses by Classification, 1908-1912]
description: Civil engineering expenditure for rivers, roads and bridges, and ports and harbours over the last five years, shown to illustrate the classification of these national outlays.

title: [Percentage of New Contracts and Dissolutions to Policy Amount at Beginning of Year]
description: Gives the new contracts and dissolutions as percentages of the policy amount at the start of each year, showing the declining ratio of new business over 1914–1916.

title: [Petroleum Production by Classes]
description: Shows annual petroleum production from 1912 to 1914 split into volatile, lamp, solar, heavy and machine oil grades, introduced by the sentence 'The production may be classified as follows'.

description: Lists the concessionaires whose mine production in 1914 exceeded or nearly reached ¥1,000,000 in value, with their values in thousands of yen.

title: [Petroleum Production by Classes]
description: Shows the annual output of petroleum by product class (volatile, lamp, solar, heavy and machine oil) for 1912 to 1914, illustrating the oil production described above.

title: Leading Concessionaires of Mines
description: Lists the mining concessionaires whose 1914 production exceeded about ¥1,000,000 in value, with their figures in thousands of yen.

description: Shows annual production values of pottery, shippo enamel ware, fire-proof and ordinary bricks, and tiles, illustrating the trade trends discussed in the text on these industries.

title: [Production of Lacquer-Juice and Lacquered Wares]
description: Gives the yearly output of lacquer-juice and lacquered wares from 1914 to 1916, presented to show production trends in the lacquer industry.

title: [Production of Sake, Beer and Soy]
description: The table gives annual output of sake, beer and soy in thousand koku for fiscal years 1913 to 1916, following the text on the brewing industries.

title: Amount and Value of Papers Produced in 1916
description: Shows the quantity and value of paper produced, exported and imported in 1916, by paper type, with pulp imports, as background to the paper industry discussion.

title: [Fish-Oil and Whale-Oil Output, 1914–1916]
description: Output of sardine, herring and whale oil in quantity and value for 1914–1916, presented to show the fish-oil industry's production.

title: [Kilowatt Capacity Classified by Enterprise and Generation, End of 1916]
description: Classifies Japan's hydro-electric kilowatt capacity by type of enterprise and generation, in operation and in preparation, as at the end of 1916.

description: Sugar refining's production and consumption estimates for Japan Proper, shown to illustrate the growing role of imports from abroad and Formosa during 1912–1916.

description: Gives the value of peppermint produced (crude, menthol, crystal oil) and exported in Japan from 1912 to 1916, illustrating the growth of the industry in Hokkaido.

title: [Productions of Straw, Chip and Hemp Braid]
description: Shows the yearly production value of straw, chip, mixed and hemp braid, illustrating the rapid growth of the braid industry from 1913 to 1916.

title: [Leather Output]
description: Shows the annual output of leather from cows and calves, horses and other sources, with totals, from 1912 to 1916, illustrating the growth of the leather industry.

title: [Hosiery Production]
description: Shows Japanese hosiery output from 1912 to 1916 by product type, illustrating the rapid growth of the Osaka-centred industry during the war years.

description: Gives the value of Japan's canned production from 1913 to 1916, broken down into beef, fish and shellfish, and fruit, to show the growth of the canning industry.

description: Lists the quantity and value of Japanese isinglass (kanten) produced for the years ended March 1914 to 1917, the export article used mainly for jam-making in Europe and America.

description: Lists the commanders of the heavy artillery brigades, by division and brigade.

description: Names the commander of the communication corps of the Guards Division, with his rank.

description: Lists the commanders, with rank and name, of each garrison, fort and independent command in the army.

description: Shows the senior officers of the Yokosuka, Kure, Sasebo and Maizuru admiralties, by post.

description: Shows the outstanding loans and debts of Chosen as of September 1916, giving the year floated, amount, interest rate and redemption period for each.

description: Lists the population of the principal cities of Taiwan at the end of 1916, in two columns.

description: Gives the annual output of principal crops in Formosa for 1913 to 1915, such as rice, rush, ground-nut, sweet potato, jute and China grass.

description: Gives the sugar cultivation area and sugar output in Formosa from 1912 to 1917, the period of rapid expansion of the industry under Government control.

description: The page describes the aborigines and lists casualties from their raids on police and others, year by year from 1909 to 1912, with killed and wounded counts.

description: Shows the December output of the principal mineral fields of Taiwan for 1914 and 1915, in thousand tsubo, as the mining section opens.

description: Shows the company's receipts and expenses by undertaking for the 1916-7 business year, with totals and profit, from the company's business report.

description: Summarises the company's business receipts and expenses by undertaking for the 1916-7 year, showing the profit earned overall.

description: Lists the principal asset and liability items of the company according to the same 1916-7 report, as given in the text.

title: Distance and Length
description: This page gives the Japanese units of distance and length with their English and metric equivalents, as a reference for readers of the Year Book.

title: Land Measures
description: This section lists Japanese land measures, from the square ri down to the tsubo and the Formosan ko, with English and metric equivalents.

title: Quantity, Capacity and Cubic Measures
description: This part gives the Japanese units of capacity and cubic measure, such as the koku, with their American and metric equivalents.

title: Weights
description: This section sets out the Japanese units of weight (kwan, kin, momme) with their avoirdupois, troy and metric equivalents.

description: This final section gives the value of the yen in sterling, United States dollars, French francs and German marks.

title: List of Mikados in Alphabetical Order
description: An alphabetical list of the Mikados (emperors) with the years each reign began and ended, giving a quick reference to the sovereigns named in the outline of Japanese history.

title: [List of the Mikados and Their Reigns]
description: The list gives the reign dates of each Mikado in order, so readers can follow the succession of sovereigns from the legendary period onward.

title: List of the Shoguns and the Regents (Shikken)
description: This list gives the years of office of the Shoguns and of the Hōjō Regents (Shikken) grouped by family, showing the succession of military rulers in Japan.

title: List of Japanese "Year-Names"
description: A chronological list of Japanese year-names (nengō) with their Japanese characters and the Western years in which each was in use, arranged alphabetically by romanized name.

title: [Table of Japanese Era Names (Nengō) with Years]
description: A reference list of Japanese era names (nengō) with their Romanized and kanji forms and the years each era covered, given for chronological lookup.

title: [Japanese Era Names with Characters and Years]
description: This page lists Japanese era names (nengō) in romanization and characters with their starting and ending Christian years, arranged in four columns for reference in the historical outline.

title: [Japanese Era Names (Nengō) with Years]
description: A list of Japanese era names (nengō) with their Romanized and kanji forms and the years each period covered, given to show the chronology of reign periods.

title: [Costs of First Instance in Civil Procedure]
description: Shows the stamp duty payable on petitions in first-instance civil suits according to the value of the subject-matter, as the text explains costs are paid by adhesive stamps.

title: Capital Punishment Classified
description: Gives the number of persons executed by capital punishment each year from 1912 to 1917, classified by the crime for which they were condemned.

title: Mutual Aid Associations of Workmen in Five Government Establishments
description: Summarises the combined mutual aid figures for five Government establishments: membership, receipts, disbursements and persons helped.

title: Data of Mutual Aid Societies of the Five Establishments
description: Gives the membership, persons helped and payments by type for each of the five establishments' mutual aid societies, following the summary figures.

title: Living Expenses of Workpeople and Petty Salary Men
description: Prof. Iwano's 1916 survey of twenty labor families gives monthly living-expense figures by category, showing that no accurate Japanese data comparable to Europe and America exists.

title: Child Operatives
description: Shows the number of child operatives under 15 in the main industries, by sex and by age group, illustrating where child labour was concentrated.

title: Number of Operatives
description: Operatives in 1917 classified by their employments, based on the Department of Agriculture and Commerce factory statistics, showing male, female and total workers by factory type.

description: Shows how many strikers and strike cases were arrested under the Peace Regulation from 1914 to 1918, with outcomes, and explains the sharp rise in 1918 linked to the rice riots.

title: Press Statistics
description: The Police Bureau's returns give the number of dailies and periodicals existing at the end of 1916 and 1917, split by whether a deposit was paid.

title: [Cost of Works Undertaken by Different Finances, 1909–10 to 1913–14]
description: Shows how the cost of river control works was borne by central government, prefectures, districts, cities, towns, villages and other bodies over five fiscal years.

description: Compares present and future annual output of pig-iron and steel materials at the leading government and private foundries in Japan proper.

description: Lists the main kinds of manufacturing industry with company counts, paid-up capital and reserves at the end of December 1917, showing where capital was concentrated.

headers: Capital p. u. for ltd. Cos.

description: Gives yearly output figures for pure sake, beer (by pint, quart and cask) and soy, showing the scale of these brewing industries from 1916 to 1918.

description: Shows production, exports and imports of shime (sheets of paper, Mino and Hanshi types) for 1917, as a second part of the paper statistics.

description: Classifies kilowatt capacity of electric enterprises as hydro or steam, in operation or in preparation, at the end of 1916.

description: The table lists the chief dye-stuffs consumed in 1918 with quantities, values and the amounts imported, showing how far domestic production covered demand.

title: Strikers Arrested Under the Peace Regulation
Legal Status of Women
description: These points of difference are enumerated in the following:—
examples: The legal restriction of age in marriage is different between men and women. According to the Civil Code of Japan, men must be above 17 years and women, 15 years.

There can be no existence of marriage without the voluntary agreement of the man and the woman when a marriage is to be contracted. If they have parents living, they must obtain their consent, unless the man has completed his 30th year and the woman her 25th. In the case of minors who have no parents alive, they must obtain the consent of their guardians and the family councils.

A woman becomes incompetent upon contracting a marriage; that is, it becomes necessary for her to obtain the permission of her husband in the conduct of important legal acts, as lending or borrowing of money, transfer of her own real estate or some valuable pieces of movable property, bringing of an action in a court of law, accepting or refusing a succession, etc.

description: Shows the output of fish oils (sardine, herring), whale oil and others, with totals, to illustrate the recent decline in the vegetable oils and waxes trade.

title: Vegetable Wax
description: Records annual production of crude and refined vegetable wax for 1919 to 1921, part of the review of declining oils and waxes.

title: Soaps
description: Gives recent soap production from leading factories by category (toilet, industrial, laundry and others), as the text introduces the leading soap makers.

title: Production
description: Shows the value of Japan's canned production by category (beef, fish and shellfish, fruit, vegetables) and total from 1919 to 1921, as background to the canning industry.

description: Shows the export destinations, by value, of the straw and chip braid goods described above, for 1919 to 1921, with the sudden 1921 drop attributed to German competition.

title: Productions
description: Gives the annual value of domestic production of straw, chip, mixed and hemp braids for 1919 to 1921, showing the total output of the braid industry.

title: Production
description: Shows Japanese hosiery production by category and total value for 1919–1921, in thousands of yen, illustrating the industry's wartime boom and postwar decline.

title: Enamelled Hard Wares
description: Shows the production and export values of enamelled hardware for 1919 to 1921 as part of the minor manufactures survey.

title: Bamboo Wares
description: Records bamboo ware production and exports for 1919 to 1921, noting that exports consist mainly of baskets, trunks and bags.

title: Fans and Folding Fans
description: Presents the production and export values of fans and folding fans for 1919 to 1921.

title: Toilet Articles
description: Gives production and export values of toilet articles for 1919 to 1921.

title: Wicker Works
description: Shows the yearly production and export values of the wicker works industry from 1919 to 1921, illustrating the trade's scale in the Industry chapter.

title: Insulated Electric Wire

description: The details of Osaka city's 1922-23 budget estimate, listing revenue and expenditure for each general and special account item.

description: Gives the dates of early and late frost and snow at each of the five stations during the year.

title: [Prefectures of Korea and Their Seats of Office]

description: Shows the yearly output of Taiwan's principal crops in 1918 to 1920, giving the country's main agricultural production figures.

title: Fruits (in 1,000 kin)
description: Gives the production of major fruits in Taiwan for 1918 to 1920, in thousands of kin.

description: Gives the value of Taiwan's trade with Japan Proper and with foreign countries, split into commodities and specie and bullion, for 1918 to 1921.

description: The estimates for the Island of Karafuto for fiscal years 1922-23 and 1923-24 are set out here, showing ordinary and extraordinary revenue and the grand total.

description: The page compares the population of the three principal cities of South Manchuria, split by sex, at the end of 1921.

description: The table reports the South Manchuria Railway's business receipts and expenses by undertaking for the 1921-22 year, showing the company's financial performance.

description: The table summarises the South Manchuria Railway's principal assets and liabilities as at 31 March 1922, giving the company's financial position.

title: Principal Crops in 1000 Chinese Koku
description: The table gives annual output of the principal crops in the Leased Territory, showing that maize was the leading crop and that most crops rose over 1919–1921.

description: Shows the number of workshops, their Japanese and Chinese employees and capital in South Manchuria for 1920, with totals for 1919 and 1918 for comparison.

description: Land area units are listed with their English and French equivalents, including the Formosan ko unit.

title: Weights
description: Japanese weight units are given with their avoirdupois and troy equivalents and their metric values.

title: Moneys
description: The yen, the Japanese monetary unit, is given with its equivalents in sterling, French francs, US dollars and German marks.

title: Formosa
description: Lists the principal mountain peaks of Formosa above 8,000 feet, with their heights in feet.

title: Korea
description: Lists the principal mountain peak of Korea above 8,000 feet, with its height in feet.

description: Following the 1920 revision of salaries, this table gives the new annual pay for principal civil and military posts in the Shin-nin rank.

title: Chokunin Rank
description: This table lists the new annual salary ranges for posts in the Chokunin rank under the revised civil and military pay scale effective from August 1920.

description: Military officers and men receive ordinary pension on retirement after 11 or more years of service, with yearly additions up to 50 years, at rates fixed by rank.

Officials of hannin rank, non-commissioned & warrant officers & privates (Yen)

description: Summarises membership and receipts of mutual aid associations of workmen in the Government Printing Bureau, Monopoly Bureau, Government Railways, naval and military workshops, and Postal Savings Bureau.

description: This continuation lists the yen amounts paid out by a relief fund under headings such as deaths, injuries, long service and medical costs, before the text on mutual aid schemes.

title: Number of Operatives
description: Operatives in factories are classified by employment and sex, giving the 1921 totals from the factory statistics compiled by the Department of Agriculture and Commerce.

headers: Average excess of exp. or overincome (Yen)

description: Breakdown of average monthly income of slum families by source, comparing the master's earnings with the wife's, as shares of income and outgo.

description: Gives the percentage of family expenditure spent on food, rent, clothing, fuel and lighting, and sundries at each income level, showing how the shares shift as income rises.

description: Breaks down the sundries item of family expenditure into its component heads, with monthly amounts per family and their share of total outgo.

description: Shows production and export values of enamelled hard wares for 1919 to 1921 as part of the minor manufactures survey.

description: Records production and export values of bamboo wares for 1919 to 1921, noting the main export goods.

title: [Restoration Works Undertaken Independently by Tokyo Municipality, Estimated at ¥23,000,000]
description: The Tokyo Municipality's own restoration works, estimated at about ¥23,000,000 over three years from 1924, to be carried out without State aid.

title: Cost of Restoration
description: Gives the money spent in 1923 on restoring the tramway system and the estimated outlay planned for 1924.

title: No. of Houses Supplied
description: Shows the number of houses supplied with water, month by month from August 1923 to May 1924, as part of the Tokyo reconstruction program's utility work.

title: Quantity Supplied
description: Gives the monthly quantity of supply, in thousands of cubic feet, from August 1923 to May 1924, accompanying the figures on houses supplied during reconstruction.

title: [Existing and Projected Streets of Yokohama]
description: Shows the street length and area of Yokohama before and after the planned reconstruction, which will widen streets and lengthen and enlarge the network by about 7 and 25 per cent.

title: [Existing and Projected Parks of Yokohama]
description: Compares the existing municipal and private parks of Yokohama with the area planned after reconstruction, as a share of the city and per inhabitant.

title: Estimate of Expenditure for 18 Months' Supply
description: The estimate gives the projected expenditure for eighteen months of reconstruction supply, covering salaries, office costs, purchases, and timber and fuel, following the Ordinance on supply.

title: Estimate for the Purchase of Goods and Materials
description: This estimate lists the quantities and values of timber, fuel, iron and steel, clothing, fish and other goods to be purchased for reconstruction.

title: Estimate of the Sale of Goods and Materials
description: This estimate lists the quantities and values of goods and materials, such as timber, iron, clothing and fish, expected to be sold or needed after the conflagration.

title: Arrivals
description: Shows the building materials that arrived for the Reconstruction Bureau, with contract quantities and values alongside the quantities and values actually received.

title: Sales
description: Lists the government's building materials sold off by the consignment firms, giving quantity and value for each material.

title: For the Whole Country
description: Gives the Government's figures for fire policies and insured amounts across the whole country in 1923, the baseline before the earthquake losses.

title: For the Affected Districts
description: Breaks down the policies and insured amounts in the affected prefectures, and then the portion of those reported as actually damaged by the earthquake fire.
headers: Of these, the following cases are reported affected

title: [Percentage of Damage by Prefecture]
description: The table shows the percentage of damage to insured policies and insurance amounts in the affected prefectures, as a share of the total.

title: List of Estimated Sympathy Payments
description: The list shows, for each insurance company, the loan advanced, its repayment term, and the estimated sympathy payments, illustrating how widely repayment terms differ between companies.

title: [Profit Percentage by Kind of Enterprise]
description: Comparing the profit percentages of the last three second-half terms across enterprise types, showing which kinds of business made losses after the earthquake.

title: Tracks and Structures
description: Shows the progress of restoration works on Government Railways lines, stations and structures as of August 20th, 1924, by line, section, work, and completion date.

title: The Circulation on January 1
description: Shows the yearly January 1 circulation of the Nichi-Nichi newspaper from 1913 to 1924, illustrating its growth to 709,000 in 1924 before the quake.

title: Schedule of Articles Exempted
description: The schedule lists the imported articles exempted from import duty, each identified by its Import Tariff number, as referred to in the remission orders above.

title: [Claims Made Under the Regulations by the End of 1923]
description: Lists the claims made under the Regulations for restoring deposits after the 1923 earthquake, by type, with counts and amounts in yen, as of the end of 1923.

title: Calendar of Annual Events
chapter: Amusements and Calendar of Annual Events
description: Below is given in chronological order a list of important annual events in Japan, including ceremonies, festivals and other national customary observances. (Dates of festivals of representative shrines are given in Chapter, XXV, Religion.)
examples: New Year's Day means as much to the Japanese as Christmas means to Western peoples, or probably more. It marks the beginning of new ilfe in an atmosphere of quiet and gaiety, leisure and pleasure. It is a time to forget the cares of the past year and enjoy feasts and indulge in all sorts of amusement in celebration of the coming good and lucky year. The homes are decorated, both inside and outside the people ar clad in their best clothes, and they all look happy.

This day is known as 'shigoto hajimé or beginning of work and is marked with ceremonies for the beginning of all sorts of activities which are to be executed properly and well in the right spirit, in the hope that everything will go on in the same happy way for the rest of the year. Carpenters begin the day by using their professional tools. Geisha tune up their samisen and practise a piece or two of music. Then first delivery of goods is undertaken by all wholesale stores in a spirit of celebration. The last named is called hatsu-ni, or first load. Cars on which goods are to be delivered on this day are fully decorated, and the carriers and delivery men, enter into the spirit of the thing, although this custom is observed in recent years with less obstentation than formerly. On the night of the second day, people were supposed, in ancient times to dream the first lucky dream of the year. To inspire such a dream, pictures representing the Seven Gods of Fortune were sold in the streets, to be placed under the pillow so that the sleeper might dream a desired dream.
The New Year holidays come to an end on this day.

title: [Enemy Strength, Operation Period and Notes of Bandit Subjugation Operations]
description: Gives the enemy strength, operation period and notes on the bandit-subjugation campaigns that the Manchoukuo forces and their allies fought in 1932.
examples: Operating jointly with the Japanese troops, drove the anti-Kirin troops to the northern parts of Kirin Province, and secured the control of the Sungari River course and occupied Ilan.

Former Tunghwa Regiment Commander Tang Chu-wu revolted, and surrounded the Japanese consulate at Tungho. Japanese Police forces advanced from Mukden, and the Fengtien Army also advanced at the same time from two different routes and commenced the clearing of the Tungpientao district. The revolting bandits being strong, Fengtien Army met defeats at various points. But the Chinganyuchitui bravely fought and demonstrated its value.
Latter part of April to the first part of July, 1932

Ma Chan-shan who ran away from Tsitsihar on April 3, gathered his former troops, and opposed the Japanese and Manchoukuo troops. The Heilungkiang Army sent two detachments and attacked the Hailun district, the base of Ma's operation, and co-operating with Japanese troops, chased the Ma forces. Confusion was caused in many parts because the attitude of the Heilungkiang Army constantly changed.

title: [Enemy Strength, Operation Periods and Notes on Bandit Operations, 1932]
description: Gives the enemy strength, operation period and a note on each bandit-suppression operation of 1932, complementing the table of Manchoukuo forces on the facing page.
examples: To subjugate the 30,000 anti-Kirin troops gathered in the district south of Harbin, the Kirin Army under the command of Lieutenant Ogawa met bandits on its way to Ssuho-cheng, after passing Yushu, and in the whole day's battle, both sides suffered much damage, and the Manchoukuo troops retreated to Yushu. The deaths among the Manchoukuo troops reached 150 including Lieutenant Ogawa, and the deaths of the enemy reached about 1,000.
The bandits under Li Hai-ching ran away to the Lanhsih district of Heilungkiang Province, and they were attacked, causing the deaths of 50 enemies; two leaders were arrested.
Latter part of June to the first part of July, 1932
Co-operating with Japanese troops, the districts of Shuangcheng, Acheng, Yushu, Wuchang and Shulan were cleared of bandits.

title: [Enemy Strength, Operation Periods and Results of Subjugation Operations]
description: Summarises the enemy strength, timing and outcome of each subjugation operation, continuing the account of the operations listed opposite.
examples: October 7 to the end of October, 1932
Co-operating with Japanese troops, made great subjugation activity in the Tungpientao district, and made Tang Wu-chen and his 1,000 subordinates surrender, while more than 270 were shot to death.
Beginning of October to the end of October, 1932

The subjugation of the Li bandits who attempted to threaten the Japanese and Manchoukuo troops from behind, in the southern part of Heilungkiang Province, scheming together with Sun Ping-wen, was made in the Anta, Chaotung, and Chaochou; the Li bandits ran away to the distant regions of Jehol Province.
To co-operate with the Japanese Independent Guard Corps in subjugating the bandits active in the square area formed by Ki-chang-Feng-Lung, troops were despatched from the Fengtien and Kirin Armies.
